decisions.question: Which calendar date goes in the stamp's `date` field ('Date: today, YYYY-MM-DD'): the UTC date or the machine's local date? The two differ at the moment of the run (UTC 2026-10-26T17:01Z, local WIB 2026-10-27 00:01).

options.label: UTC date
options.consequence: The stamp reads 2026-10-26, consistent with the `date -u` timestamps every report and ledger line carries.

options.label: Local date
options.consequence: The stamp reads 2026-10-27, which is the owner's calendar day but disagrees with every UTC timestamp written in the same step.

decisions.why: The preamble takes every timestamp from `date -u`, and docs/auto-run/timestamp-corrections.md records what went wrong when local time was labelled UTC. A single clock for the stamp and the report avoids a one-day disagreement inside one step. The skill only says 'today'. A rule that governance dates are the owner's local calendar day would have changed my mind.

decisions.question: The self-contained gate (Rule 2: 'Every contract, ADR and OQ id the file names has its text inline in its section. Other phases' ids appear only in the Phase block's Dependencies and Collides with lines') flags ids that occur only inside verbatim excerpts: 8 contract ids (bus-api@v2, flutter-binding@v2, navigation-api@v1, nidana-checks@v1, topic-codegen@v1, topic-model@v1, topology-dsl@v2, topology-ir@v1), 5 OQ ids (OQ8, OQ9, OQ12, OQ-T2, OQ-F1) and 7 other-phase ids (nidana.flutter.1, nidana.model.2 to .7 outside Dependencies and Collides with). How does the rule apply?

options.label: Apply the gate to ids the file selects; excerpt-internal citations stay as the source's words
options.consequence: ADR-001 and ADR-002, the only ids at structural positions (Governed by, Decisions headings, Links), are inline. The flagged ids stay inside the excerpts that cite them, unchanged and uninlined; the file carries no contract section because the phase consumes and produces none.

options.label: Inline every cited contract and OQ
options.consequence: Pulls eight contracts and five OQ rows the phase neither consumes, produces nor cites, contradicting the Contracts and Open questions selection rules and the 'too large signals a phase that touches too much' rule.

options.label: Paraphrase or drop the excerpt text that carries the ids
options.consequence: Passes a literal gate but breaks Rule 1 (no summary, no dropped line) and the task's explicit instruction.

options.label: Stop and ask
options.consequence: Ends the step; the task has already told me to decide and record this case.

decisions.chosen: Apply the gate to ids the file selects; excerpt-internal citations stay as the source's words
decisions.why: The skill's own selection rules (Contracts: only those the phase's Consumes or Produces names; Open questions: only those the phase or its contracts cite) and Rule 1 (verbatim, no truncation) cannot all hold under a reading of Rule 2 that counts every id inside a mandated excerpt, because the node's Owns and Isolation strategy fields and the ADR Decision text name contracts and phases the phase has nothing to do with. The check script (scratchpad, not a repo file) classified every occurrence by region: the structural positions hold ADR-001 and ADR-002 only, both inline. Rule 2's other-phase clause is violated by the same kind of text, including the phase's own verbatim Scope (nidana.flutter.1). A skill wording that scoped Rule 2 to selected ids, or told the writer to inline cited contracts, would have changed my mind.
